title: Degrees Latitude to Kilometers Calculator
description: Convert degrees of latitude to kilometres with the Degrees Latitude to Kilometers Calculator — the near-constant 111 km, refined by latitude. Free.
summary_sentence: For example, the 0.1167 degrees of latitude between Times Square and JFK is 12.96 km of north-south ground — latitude's degree is the most dependable ruler on the map.
quick_answer: The Degrees Latitude to Kilometers Calculator converts a difference in latitude into the north-south ground distance it represents, using WGS84's degree length at the relevant latitude. Enter the degrees and read kilometres (or miles) — latitude's ruler, accurate to the ellipsoid's gentle variation between equator and pole.

faq: Is one degree always exactly the same distance?

Not exactly — it grows about 1% from equator (110.574 km) to pole (111.694 km) because the Earth is an oblate ellipsoid. The calculator applies the latitude's own length; the flat 111 km rule is fine for estimates.
Is it good for surveying?
The conversion is ellipsoid-true; surveying additionally lives on local datums, heights and field method. For planning, checking and learning, this accuracy is the real thing.
Which datum do these coordinate tools use?
WGS84, the frame web maps and GPS share — tile and pixel systems on this page are defined over it.
Do more decimal places always mean better accuracy?
No — pixels and tiles quantise the world; extra coordinate decimals beyond the cell size are decoration.
Can I copy the result into GIS software?
Distances are numbers, welcome everywhere; the coordinates they came from paste as themselves.
Miles?
Both units, per this site's convention — 1° of latitude is roughly 69 miles, the number American road atlases quietly assume.
South latitude differences?
Signs take care of themselves — a span from −10° to −25° is 15° of southern latitude, priced like its northern twin.
Tiny fractions?
0.001° ≈ 111 m; 0.0001° ≈ 11 m — the precision family's ladder restated in degree language.
Difference between two latitudes directly?
Subtract the latitudes, convert the difference — for spans crossing the equator, the calculator's latitude input wants the mid-latitude of the span.
Why does it grow toward the poles?
The meridian's radius of curvature increases as the ellipsoid flattens — geometry, visible in the table's gentle slope.
